replies.author: JustAnotherBoringNPC
replies.body: Yeah, I make multiplayer games on steam. I've made quiet a few aswell. However the most players Ive allowed is 9 per match. For most games it's about 4. I feel like your network optimization has to be on fucking point for an mmo to reduce bandwidth usage and I just don't think I'm good enough with network optimization to reduce bandwidth usage per player enough to support 100+ people. (Cuz if your network optimization sucks = how much you have to pay for server costs per player. For dedicated servers anyways. All of my games I've used are peer to peer up until this point.

replies.author: JustAnotherBoringNPC
replies.body:
It would be a dream to create an mmo... I say dream because making an mmo would also be a nightmare of a project
.

replies.body: All right cool, I have quite a bit of unused server resources on my current dedicated server, so we'll see how it works out. I have no idea really, but I am not worrying about 100 concurrent players until i can get 10.

comments.author: trashcanhat
comments.body: What were you using to make the 3d models towards the end of the video?

replies.author: alekblom
replies.body: first [https://gemini.google.com/](https://gemini.google.com/) for images then feed those images to [https://studio.tripo3d.ai/](https://studio.tripo3d.ai/) for the lowpoly 3d models. Then they go into Blender for touch up, rigging, animation.

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body: do you rig yourself? I have been using meshy for both model creation & simple rigging

replies.author: alekblom
replies.body: The Mushroom Man in the video was rigged and animated with Tripo 3D. The spider, it failed partly on rigging so had to add a few more bones and the animations manually. For simple creatures like a sludge, birds and such I just do it manually as it is probably quicker than AI generating it and fixing it.
